currentContext.business: Deepak Nitrite Limited ('DNL') is a chemical manufacturing public limited company incorporated and domiciled in India, with its registered office at Vadodara, Gujarat and manufacturing facilities in the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Telangana. The Company manufactures Advanced Intermediates, which are used in agrochemicals, dyes, pharmaceuticals and personal care products, and it operates multi-purpose plants that allow flexibility in allocating capacity toward high-demand applications. Growth is anchored in value-chain integration and speciality chemical expansion, supported by a centralised R&D centre and pilot-plant infrastructure that bridges laboratory work and commercial production.

currentContext.expansion:
FY 2025-26 was a build-out year centred on backward integration at Dahej. Deepak achieved what the Directors' Report calls a major milestone with the successful commissioning, stabilisation and ramp-up of Deepak Chem Tech's nitration and hydrogenation facilities at Dahej, projects management says enhance raw material security, reduce external dependency, improve structural cost competitiveness and strengthen its positioning as a deeply integrated chemical manufacturer. A further milestone was the commissioning of Deepak's Nitric Acid plant, which has laid the foundation for commissioning of present and future nitration-based products on a fully sustainable platform. Alongside these, the commissioning of various debottlenecking initiatives through the year led to gains in production capacity for several key intermediates, with capacity expansion pursued both greenfield and brownfield.

The forward pipeline has two named legs. The multipurpose agrochemical intermediates project and the MIBC (Methyl Isobutyl Carbinol) and MIBK (Methyl Isobutyl Ketone) projects made steady progress during the year and are scheduled for commissioning in Q2 of FY 2026-27. Separately, execution of a fully integrated polycarbonate facility — described as a first for India — is stated to be on track; for this project Deepak Chem Tech Limited has entered into a strategic long-term agreement to establish a dedicated on-site HyCO plant at its Dahej facility under a 'Build-Own-Operate' model, under which the Operating Company will manage the dedicated on-site infrastructure, allowing Deepak to keep a sharp focus on the polycarbonate resin project while enhancing execution visibility, reducing upfront investment and improving supply chain resilience.

On the innovation side, the Company commissioned a state-of-the-art Research & Development Centre with an investment exceeding Rs 100 Crores (the DRDC at Savli, Vadodara), described as the strong R&D support underpinning the Company's 'future ready' positioning.

On energy and utilities, total capex and investments of Rs 18.13 Crores were approved relating to energy conservation in FY 2025-26. The Company has entered into long-term group captive agreements for procurement of renewable power for facilities in the Gujarat and Maharashtra region which, upon commissioning, are expected to replace approximately 70% of conventional power consumption with renewable energy. Renewable power sourcing has already been operationalised at the Nandesari, Dahej and Roha facilities, replacing about 20% of conventional electricity consumption, with approximately 20.6 million units procured from renewable sources during the year; this momentum is expected to continue through enhanced renewable power substitution at existing plants and expansion to additional facilities in FY 2026-27. Site-level efficiency projects were executed at Hyderabad (agitator redesign with VFDs; RO pre-treatment optimisation cutting backwash water to the ZLD system by about 60%), Nandesari (distillation column optimisation, cooling tower interconnection, pinch-analysis heat integration underway, impeller trimming and coating cutting power consumption 3-10%, energy-efficient cooling tower fan), Dahej (125 W HPMV fixtures replaced with 45 W LEDs, ATFD vapour heat recovery into the MEE system, high-efficiency surface aerator) and Roha (VFDs on ETP air blowers).

risks.risk: Climate change and emissions exposure inherent to energy- and water-intensive chemical production
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR materiality assessment as a Risk with negative financial implications if unaddressed. Management states that given the energy and water-intensive nature of chemical production, failure to reduce the environmental footprint can have significant repercussions on standing within the industry and on relationships with customers, investors and society. Physical as well as transition climate risks are described as directly associated with disruptions to the Company's operations and those of its value chain partners. Mitigation is via sustainable manufacturing practices, reducing utility consumption, extracting value from waste, adopting clean technologies and keeping effluents, emissions and waste within Pollution Control Board limits.

risks.risk: Occupational health, safety and process-safety incidents
risks.note: Flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Given the inherent nature of operations, employees face a range of operational and safety hazards; process safety gaps and OHS incidents could harm employees, jeopardise production targets and adversely affect assets, environment and business reputation. Mitigated through stringent site-level safety measures, regular safety audits, provision of appropriate PPE, and safety awareness campaigns and training.

risks.risk: Corporate governance and regulatory compliance failure
risks.note: Flagged as a Risk. Amid escalating macro-economic volatility in the chemical industry, meeting regulatory compliance requirements and effectively managing risk is described as paramount; failure would have severe financial implications, since governance is increasingly the parameter for evaluation by external stakeholders. Mitigation rests on the Board's composition and independent thinking, a robust code of conduct, a comprehensive risk management framework and focused Board Committees (Audit, Risk Management, Nomination and Remuneration, CSR, Sustainability), supported by a legal compliance management tool that tracks compliance across factories and offices with automatic regulatory updates.

Explicitly identified as a Risk in the BRSR materiality table — having a sustainable supply chain is described as critical for the Company's operations and business continuity given the size of the Company's supplier base (the disclosure is truncated in the routed source).

risks.risk: Product stewardship — reputational damage and market-share loss from ESG impacts of products
risks.note: Classified as both Risk and Opportunity: the stated risk is reputational damage and negative impact on market share. DNL has established a protocol to assess the ESG impacts of products during their development stages, has calculated the carbon footprint for most of its products and plans to conduct Life Cycle Assessments for a few existing products.

risks.risk: Chinese dumping and subdued agrochemical demand compressing realisations
risks.note: The Directors' Report states the Company faced subdued demand in select agrochemicals products due to sluggish global and domestic consumption, accompanied by pressure on realisation due to sustained dumping by Chinese suppliers — a structural pricing overhang on a core end-market.

risks.risk: Raw material cost swings, feedstock/crude volatility and tightening environmental norms
risks.note: Management states it remained alert to external pressures including raw material cost swings and tightening environmental norms, responding with proactive sourcing diversification, operational optimisation and enhanced customer focus. The FY26 fourth quarter saw disruption in established supply chains, logistics and freight challenges with the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz, leading to scarcity in availability and volatility in prices of crude oil and related feedstocks.

risks.risk: Global trade-policy shifts and tariff measures affecting export competitiveness
risks.note: The tariff measures announced by the U.S. administration reshaped trade patterns across chemicals; while direct impact on the Company's operations remained limited due to its focus on import substitution, a diversified portfolio and balanced market presence, these measures influenced global pricing, customer procurement strategies and export competitiveness in certain product segments, and changed competitive intensity, demand patterns and investment decisions.

one-line thesis: Deepak Nitrite leveraged strategic feedstock inventory builds ahead of Middle East tensions to drive a 74% QoQ EBITDA surge in Q4FY26, offsetting technical teething issues in new nitric acid capacity. The thesis pivots on FY27 margin expansion from new agro-chemical products and the long-term value unlock of the integrated polycarbonate complex commissioned by 2028.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,127 Cr (Q4), INR 7,947 Cr (FY26); down YoY due to price/volume mix but up 7% QoQ. EBITDA: INR 383 Cr (Q4, 18% margin) vs INR 219 Cr (Q3); FY26 EBITDA INR 1,041 Cr. PAT: INR 220 Cr (Q4, +120% QoQ, +9% YoY); FY26 PAT INR 551 Cr. One-offs: FY26 PBT excludes INR 91 Cr dividend income; FY25 had INR 13 Cr land gain. Order Book: Not applicable (commodity/specialty chemical spot & contract sales). Net Debt: Healthy balance sheet with INR 5,869 Cr net worth; funding secured for INR 11,000 Cr capex via 60:40 debt-equity.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Q1FY27 expected to be better than Q4FY26 on both standalone and consolidated basis. Margins: FY27 to see stronger margin profile driven by new high-margin products and normalization. Order Inflow: Stable domestic demand; export recovery expected as logistics normalize. Capex: INR 11,000 Cr total program; Polycarbonate commissioning targeted June 2028; MIBK/MIBC commissioning Q1/Q2 FY27.
order book & pipeline: N/A (Make-to-stock/order model); however, management highlights 'wallet share' retention and stable domestic supply commitments replacing import dependency for customers.
segment / subsidiary detail: Advanced Intermediates: Rev INR 708 Cr (+8% YoY), EBIT INR 34 Cr (vs INR 15 Cr Q3); driven by optimized mix. Phenolics: Rev INR 1,429 Cr, EBIT INR 287 Cr (20% margin); benefited from stable ops and improved spreads despite feedstock volatility.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) MIBK/MIBC commissioning in Q1/Q2 FY27. 2) 6-7 new agrochemical/custom molecules reaching commercial scale by Q3 FY27. 3) Fluorinated molecule plant (INR 220 Cr) validation complete, regular production Q3 FY27. 4) India's first fully integrated Polycarbonate facility (June 2028).
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 margins (18%) boosted by proactive low-cost feedstock procurement (benzene, xylene, toluene) ahead of geopolitical spikes. Cost headwinds noted in sulfur downstream (sulfuric acid/Oleum), but net impact neutralized by nitration chemistry tailwinds from Chinese regulatory constraints.
capex / expansion: Total program ~INR 11,000 Cr. Key projects: Polycarbonate complex (INR 5,000+ Cr component), Nitration/Hydrogenation (commissioned/stabilizing), MIBK/MIBC, Fluorinated molecules. Funding: 60% debt (tied up), 40% equity (internal accruals + market if needed).
capital allocation: Final dividend INR 7.5/share recommended. Reinvestment priority on backward integration (HyCO plant with Praxair) and downstream polymerization to capture value chain spread. Debt drawdown linked to equity infusion milestones (25% equity for 40% debt tranche).
risks & watch-items: 1) Technical stability of new Concentrated Nitric Acid (CNA) plant (ran at 45% util in Q4 due to issues). 2) Geopolitical escalation affecting Strait of Hormuz logistics. 3) Chinese regulatory enforcement timing/intensity. 4) Sulfur cost inflation.
management quality / tone: Confident and opportunistic; emphasized 'agility' in supply chain management and 'structural' advantages of integration. Transparent on CNA technical glitches but firm on FY27 improvement trajectory.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly linked Q4 margin beat to a contrarian 'buy every dip' feedstock strategy initiated in Jan/Feb based on US aircraft carrier movements, creating an inventory buffer that paid off during Q4 price spikes. Also, the Polycarbonate project uses a 'Build-Own-Operate' model with Praxair for HyCO to reduce upfront capex and execution risk.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Deepak Nitrite Limited is a Vadodara-headquartered chemical manufacturer of Advanced Intermediates, pursuing a deeply integrated chemical and petrochemical platform anchored in value-chain integration, import substitution and in-house R&D.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Deepak Nitrite Limited ('DNL') is a chemical manufacturing public limited company incorporated and domiciled in India, with its registered office at Vadodara, Gujarat and manufacturing facilities in the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Telangana. The Company manufactures Advanced Intermediates, which are used in agrochemicals, dyes, pharmaceuticals and personal care products, and it operates multi-purpose plants that allow flexibility in allocating capacity toward high-demand applications. Growth is anchored in value-chain integration and speciality chemical expansion, supported by a centralised R&D centre and pilot-plant infrastructure that bridges laboratory work and commercial production.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Advanced Intermediates: Rev INR 708 Cr (+8% YoY), EBIT INR 34 Cr (vs INR 15 Cr Q3); driven by optimized mix. Phenolics: Rev INR 1,429 Cr, EBIT INR 287 Cr (20% margin); benefited from stable ops and improved spreads despite feedstock volatility.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Q1FY27 expected to be better than Q4FY26 on both standalone and consolidated basis. Margins: FY27 to see stronger margin profile driven by new high-margin products and normalization. Order Inflow: Stable domestic demand; export recovery expected as logistics normalize. Capex: INR 11,000 Cr total program; Polycarbonate commissioning targeted June 2028; MIBK/MIBC commissioning Q1/Q2 FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 1) MIBK/MIBC commissioning in Q1/Q2 FY27. 2) 6-7 new agrochemical/custom molecules reaching commercial scale by Q3 FY27. 3) Fluorinated molecule plant (INR 220 Cr) validation complete, regular production Q3 FY27. 4) India's first fully integrated Polycarbonate facility (June 2028).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global growth is projected at approximately 3.1% (Source: IMF, April 2026), indicating a moderate but slowing trajectory, with inflation above target in several major economies keeping interest rates elevated and investment activity reduced
- India is projected to grow GDP at approximately 6.5% in 2026 (Source: IMF, April 2026), driven by robust domestic demand, sustained public investment in infrastructure and a vibrant services sector
- The global chemical industry is in structural adjustment after a prolonged downturn between 2022 and 2025 (Source: McKinsey), facing subdued demand, persistent overcapacity and elevated cost pressures; growth is expected to remain modest at approximately 2-3% annually (Source: Oliver Wyman) with production expanding at around 2% per year (Source: Deloitte)
- Sector competitiveness will increasingly depend on cost discipline, supply chain resilience and a strategic shift toward Speciality and high-value chemical segments that offer structurally stronger margins and more stable demand profiles
- India's chemical industry contributes nearly 7% to GDP with a product base spanning over 80,000 products (Source: IBEF); the sector is expected to be $400 billion in the near term and poised to be $1.00 trillion by 2040
- India's chemical trade deficit, estimated at approximately $31 billion (Source: McKinsey), particularly in polymers and inorganics, presents a strong case for import substitution and domestic capacity expansion
- Emerging sectors such as electric vehicles, renewable energy, semiconductors and infrastructure are expected to drive incremental demand, reinforcing India's position as a future global hub for chemical manufacturing
- Near-term headwinds cited by management: over-capacity particularly from China and pricing pressures; the Advanced Intermediates business operated amid a tariff war and Middle-East conflict leading to subdued global demand
- Offsetting levers cited by management: deeper customer focus, volume growth, improved operational efficiencies, prudent financial management, improved competitiveness through enhanced integration, product mix optimisation and customer-centric execution
- Outlook framing: global supply chains are being reconfigured and customers increasingly seek reliable, diversified sourcing partners; while near-term uncertainties may persist, the long-term outlook remains firmly positive with confidence in delivering sustainable growth and improved profitability

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 margins (18%) boosted by proactive low-cost feedstock procurement (benzene, xylene, toluene) ahead of geopolitical spikes. Cost headwinds noted in sulfur downstream (sulfuric acid/Oleum), but net impact neutralized by nitration chemistry tailwinds from Chinese regulatory constraints.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Final dividend INR 7.5/share recommended. Reinvestment priority on backward integration (HyCO plant with Praxair) and downstream polymerization to capture value chain spread. Debt drawdown linked to equity infusion milestones (25% equity for 40% debt tranche).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body:
FY 2025-26 was a build-out year centred on backward integration at Dahej. Deepak achieved what the Directors' Report calls a major milestone with the successful commissioning, stabilisation and ramp-up of Deepak Chem Tech's nitration and hydrogenation facilities at Dahej, projects management says enhance raw material security, reduce external dependency, improve structural cost competitiveness and strengthen its positioning as a deeply integrated chemical manufacturer. A further milestone was the commissioning of Deepak's Nitric Acid plant, which has laid the foundation for commissioning of present and future nitration-based products on a fully sustainable platform. Alongside these, the commissioning of various debottlenecking initiatives through the year led to gains in production capacity for several key intermediates, with capacity expansion pursued both greenfield and brownfield.

The forward pipeline has two named legs. The multipurpose agrochemical intermediates project and the MIBC (Methyl Isobutyl Carbinol) and MIBK (Methyl Isobutyl Ketone) projects made steady progress during the year and are scheduled for commissioning in Q2 of FY 2026-27. Separately, execution of a fully integrated polycarbonate facility — described as a first for India — is stated to be on track; for this project Deepak Chem Tech Limited has entered into a strategic long-term agreement to establish a dedicated on-site HyCO plant at its Dahej facility under a 'Build-Own-Operate' model, under which the Operating Company will manage the dedicated on-site infrastructure, allowing Deepak to keep a sharp focus on the polycarbonate resin project while enhancing execution visibility, reducing upfront investment and improving supply chain resilience.

On the innovation side, the Company commissioned a state-of-the-art Research & Development Centre with an investment exceeding Rs 100 Crores (the DRDC at Savli, Vadodara), described as the strong R&D support underpinning the Company's 'future ready' positioning.

On energy and utilities, total capex and investments of Rs 18.13 Crores were approved relating to energy conservation in FY 2025-26. The Company has entered into long-term group captive agreements for procurement of renewable power for facilities in the Gujarat and Maharashtra region which, upon commissioning, are expected to replace approximately 70% of conventional power consumption with renewable energy. Renewable power sourcing has already been operationalised at the Nandesari, Dahej and Roha facilities, replacing about 20% of conventional electricity consumption, with approximately 20.6 million units procured from renewable sources during the year; this momentum is expected to continue through enhanced renewable power substitution at existing plants and expansion to additional facilities in FY 2026-27. Site-level efficiency projects were executed at Hyderabad (agitator redesign with VFDs; RO pre-treatment optimisation cutting backwash water to the ZLD system by about 60%), Nandesari (distillation column optimisation, cooling tower interconnection, pinch-analysis heat integration underway, impeller trimming and coating cutting power consumption 3-10%, energy-efficient cooling tower fan), Dahej (125 W HPMV fixtures replaced with 45 W LEDs, ATFD vapour heat recovery into the MEE system, high-efficiency surface aerator) and Roha (VFDs on ETP air blowers).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and opportunistic; emphasized 'agility' in supply chain management and 'structural' advantages of integration. Transparent on CNA technical glitches but firm on FY27 improvement trajectory.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Centralised R&D moat: DRDC at Savli with a dedicated team of 103 professionals; the Company has cumulatively filed around 86 patent applications, of which 26 patents have already been granted
- New world-class DRDC at Savli (operational since October 2025) covering synthesis, analytical development, process engineering and safety labs, scale-up plant and an environment lab — designed to handle complex chemistries such as high pressure-high temperature and oxidation reactions
- Two advanced pilot plants at Roha and Nandesari that bridge R&D and commercial production, enabling seamless scale-up of intermediates
- Advanced process control (APC) systems and a dedicated process-safety team with in-house ARC, DSC and reaction calorimetry capability
- Multi-purpose plants providing flexibility to reallocate capacity to high-demand applications and ensure efficient utilisation
- Execution track record, manufacturing expertise, deep customer relationships and commitment to value-added chemistry
- Relentless focus on import substitution and a diversified product portfolio, which limited the direct impact of U.S. tariff measures on operations
- Academic and research collaborations with IIT Bombay, ICT Mumbai, IICT Hyderabad, NCL Pune, CSMCRI Bhavnagar, Dharmsinh Desai University, M.S. University and GSFC University
- Integration milestones at Dahej (nitration, hydrogenation and Nitric Acid) that enhance raw material security and reduce external dependency

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Technical stability of new Concentrated Nitric Acid (CNA) plant (ran at 45% util in Q4 due to issues). 2) Geopolitical escalation affecting Strait of Hormuz logistics. 3) Chinese regulatory enforcement timing/intensity. 4) Sulfur cost inflation.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly linked Q4 margin beat to a contrarian 'buy every dip' feedstock strategy initiated in Jan/Feb based on US aircraft carrier movements, creating an inventory buffer that paid off during Q4 price spikes. Also, the Polycarbonate project uses a 'Build-Own-Operate' model with Praxair for HyCO to reduce upfront capex and execution risk.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Anchor strategic direction in value chain integration, expansion into Speciality and performance chemicals, and innovation-led differentiation — transitioning 'from scale to value creation'
- Consolidate the position across the ammonia-nitration-amines value chain, which the Company says places it among a select group of global players with such integrated capabilities and gives greater control over critical inputs
- Move toward high-value, application-driven downstream segments through the MIBK/MIBC projects and the polycarbonate initiative, aligned with India's aspiration for self-reliance in …

challenges.body:

| High freight costs and supply chain disruption from Middle East conflict blocking Strait of Hormuz; working capital blockage in imports. | Deepak Nitrite Ltd | beneficiary | High | Domestic customers shifting to Deepak for JIT supply to avoid import volatility; company captured margin upside via low-cost inventory while competitors faced spot price spikes. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group vs listed entity] Several strategy claims and the entire CMD message are framed around 'Deepak Group', and the Polycarbonate build is described as 'DCTL's Polycarbonate project' - not explicitly attributed to the listed entity Deepak Nitrite Limited on a standalone basis.
- [Structure] Manufacturing sites are attributed to multiple entities - DNL, DCTL, DAML, DPL, DCLT (as printed, for Sankarda) and DOIL (Oman) - with no shareholding or consolidation map provided.
- [Digitalisation] 'Digital initiatives include SAP S/4HANA migration, AI/ML-driven smart manufacturing, optimize power and predictive analytics through a Digital Innovation Lab'.
- [Regulatory] Growth drivers cite alignment with 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' for import substitution, benefit from PCPIR infrastructure, and 'Strong Government backing'.
- [Disruption landscape] Named headwinds: geopolitical tensions and shifting trade dynamics, aggressive global (especially China-led) pricing, logistics disruptions and freight volatility, feedstock constraints, energy cost volatility and 'Potential demand softness'.
